reviews.review_text: I've never written my own review but I feel compelled to do so when it comes to these apartments.. I normally always read reviews before ever making a decision but in this case I was referred by a friend who's opinion is normally right on point. Don't make the same mistake as me!! Read the reviews anyway!! When we first got here and were given the tour the place looked pretty and I loved the floor model. When we moved in we were overall very happy with the appearance of our unit. We had just got brand new carpets and the bathrooms and kitchen had wood flooring (fake wood but we still liked it better than the lenolium tile). Ill start with the smaller things that really didnt bother me too much but may bother other people. Within a few weeks of living here we notices the problems they had with the water. There's no pressure and both of our toilets clogged up at the same time as well as our kitchen sink. The toilets were an easy fix with a plunger but the sink we had to wait for maintenance who took two days to come.. Again not that big of a deal they came and fixed it but it was frustrating to have to use our bathroom sinks to wash things. For anyone who lives near the pool I am so sorry. It's a 24 hr pool which you would think is a nice ammenity but when your bedroom patio door is facing the pool and there's constantly people partying down there all night.. Not so fun. But again this is minuscule to what I'm about to get into.. However it's a shame that the pool has been closed several times due to people taking a crap in the water or getting glass from their glass beer bottles in the pool. When we first moved in there was a free online rent payment when the management was still udr.. they changed management and now its a $33 fee to pay with a credit card, $10 fee when u pay with a checking account (and this id everytime u pay) or free for automatic payments which is frustrating because not everyone can or wants to do this. Now for the entire reason I'm actually taking the time to write this review.. After being here about 4 months I started noticing that my 1 yr old daughter was getting bit. A lot. I figured its summer and we live by the pool it's probably Mosquitos. But it was strange that I never saw them in my apartment. One day when my fianc  was taking out the trash (a mile away from our unit it seems like) there was a couch with the words bed bugs spray painted on it. I had never had a bed bug experience or really ever knew much about them so it's not something I ever would've thought about. But it triggered me to go look at the reviews. Upon typing in "finisterra" the first thing in google I saw said "bed bugs".. Funny though that these are now the only reviews I can find. So this is when I decided to start checking my daughters room and monitoring her bites more. I always check on my kids before I go to bed and one night I went in there and went to adjust her and noticed blood on her sheets and called in her dad to get a second set of eyes. He started moving her sheets to look for more and there it was.. A live bed bug. DISGUSTING!! We immediately pulled her out of her bed and started searching her bed. Along the inside of the lining of her sheet was a group of about 7 bed bugs. We wrapped her sheets up and trashed them killed the one we found and left it for the apartments to see. The next day we noticed out neighbors getting pest treatment. Our apartment is attached to our neighbors at my daughters room. Called the office got the treatment for free which was a nuisance because it consists of bagging and washing alllllll the linens for two full weeks. We got the all clear at the follow up inspection and all seemed calm in the world again. Until now...3 months later and they are back. Only this time the office has informed us that our treatment would be at our own cost. They basically told us we have to prove we are not the source.. Let me tell you.. We didn't have a problem again until our same neighbors were getting their carpets ripped out. But we heard two different stories from the office as to why they were getting ripped out. One said it was for roaches (yep there are roaches here too) and one said because the carpets were thrashed. Here's the thing. With as many reviews online about the bed bugs at this place and the fact they do routine pest inspections here.. They know they're the source. I've had to throw away my bed, and my baby's brand new bassinet to try and help the matter on my own. Now I've decided that I won't live here with my two children and am paying almost $3000 to get out of my lease plus what's it's going to cost me to buy all new furniture... Do yourself a favor... Go somewhere else!

reviews.review_text:
Everything was great for the first four to six months living here. After that things started to decline. 

CONS:Our next door neighbors got robbed, to confirm this you can see the newscast online by searching "robbery caught on camera by video game" and watch the one with the Asian girl. Then tempe PD woke us up a week later at midnight when I was sick with the flu and made us leave for three hours. A month or so later the office had our buildings painted and the painters broke two of my patio chairs. I left multiple voicemails to the office regarding my broken chairs but heard nothing back...ever! I guess they figured my renters insurance would take care of it and they couldn't be bothered. Maintainence took three days to change a light bulb in our kitchen then shortly after the other one went out and we have just dealt with it rather than wait for them again. They also barged into our apartment while I was sleeping, jimmied my LOCKED bedroom door open and demanded that I wake up so they could check my faucet for thirty seconds. No regard for the tenants' property or privacy whatsoever. Waking a tenant up to check a faucet is unacceptable. Wait another hour, make a phone call, come back later but don't break into a locked bedroom with the half naked tenant asleep within and demand to see the faucet. And last but not least the spa has had about a pound of dirt in the bottom of it for the past 10 months and no one has bothered to clean it out. The gates keep breaking and the gate on our end of the complex was broken for six months, causing us to drive to the front end of the complex and exit near the office. When your complex only had two gates, it shouldn't even be an option to let one sit broken for six months.

Some PROS: The unique floor plan makes the living room feel huge. The apartment was clean and ready upon move in. The clubhouse and fitness center are always clean and great. The community is USUALLY very quiet though the occasional Indian guy can be heard on his phone at 3am-5am talking to his relatives in Bangladesh or wherever but that's anywhere you go. The grounds are kept quite clean except for the aforementioned dirt in the spa.

OVERALL SUMMARY: The unique floor plan and clean grounds make you feel like you've gotten a steal for your money until you have any sort of issue, especially major ones. Management seems only to care about...well nothing really. They'll say or do anything for you the first couple of months then they treat you like crap and let their maintenence staff destroy your property and sleep schedule. Community isn't very safe despite the gates as you can tell from the robbery. Overall, the nice-ish apartment is not worth all the hassle and complete lack of respect you will experience living here.

reviews.review_text:
What originally brought me to moving into this complex was because they have glass-top stove ranges instead of the coiled (easier to clean) and because they have a washer/dryer in every unit. It looked like it was the best in the area that was close to my work. I was completely WRONG. Upon move-in, many of our appliances were broken  (bathtub had little to no water pressure and gave freezing cold water, the micro-hood was totaled, and the fridge would leak excessively) and it took maintenance forever to replace or fix them, despite all of my requests. The walkways throughout the complex are VERY easy to slip and trip on (especially if the walkways are wet by the sprinklers). Parking is very crammed, people rarely use the special covered parking because the spaces are too crammed to make at least one side of the car impossible to open the doors to. The streets are too narrow; it's barley enough room for 2 cars going opposite directions to fit onto. Security is okay, but the general neighborhood has several emergency phone calls and during my 14 months here, the area of the complex in which I live has been flooded with cops several times. The walls are whatnot are also very thin. That, or the neighbors are just too big of party people. I personally don't mind loud neighbors, but if you don't like them, I would be cautious.  

Other than constantly having to have maintenance come out to our apartment, we also had to have our cable company (Cox) come to re-wire out internet/television connection because it was poorly done, causing our cable to constantly become intermittent. About 6 or so months after we moved in, the staff started giving everyone of the tenants notices about a pest infestation (bedbugs/roaches) and how they were going to inspect each of the apartments to see if any of them were infected. Our apartment was conveniently skipped, but our building had a cockroach issue. My family and I are very cleanly, but no matter how clean there would still be roaches coming out of the kitchen sink and whatnot. I called the staff about them missing my apartment, and how we have a cockroach issue that needed to be tended to, and while the staff appeared friendly it took them several months to bring a pest maintenance guy out to even "inspect" the apartment, and now about 2 weeks before we move out, they want to do a fog of the apartment which should have been done months ago. Go figure, they'll wait till the apartment nearly becomes available to make it look as nice as possible for the next poor people to bother signing a lease with this place. 

The rent is too expensive for poor service, constantly breaking appliances, and for anything else I mentioned in my review. I'm glad I will be leaving this place soon.

reviews.review_text: I know people read reviews on apartments before moving in or going to see and then think well maybe they are just disgruntled people. Actually what I have read on here for the awful reviews are true, so please believe them when you read them. I lived in these apartments for basically three years. At first the place was great, office people were great and maintenance was AWESOME! Then the changes came. The office people were changed, this happens like clockwork, think we went through about six or more changes while we were there and the property manager was changed. The new manager had not a clue what he was doing, and the new office people didn't seem to get it or have a clue or maybe it was they just didn't care. The maintenance people are shuffled between I think three other complexes trying to keep up with repairs. This is impossible for them to do and you never get the same one after you waited your three weeks to have them come. YEP, three weeks was the last count I heard from one of them (who was smart and left)that they are behind. The office manager that came on board and was the start of the place being destroyed is now working as the maintenance manager, wonder why the maintenance is so bad. Let's move on, the front security gates are usually open pretty much of the time because they are broken most of the time and they don't want to pay for the repairs to them anymore so this allows for anyone to walk in. If they aren't open there's a small wooden gate that anyone can walk through further in the back and that's always open so anyone can get into the complex, so when they say secured it's not. There use to be security officers that were on after 10pm until like 4 or 5am but they got rid of them too. They have ground people that come to mow the lawn like two times a week and they arrive at about 6:15 to 6:30am and start with their loud noise, you can't sleep or even hear yourself think when they start. The pool itself is pretty nasty most of the time,but there are two, that are the same way. They also have a lock to get in and out of the pool, doesn't seem to safe to be locked inside the pool and can't get out. Just my opinion on safety. The fitness room is small and doesn't have a lot of equipment,even less when it's broken which is most of the time. Now let's talk about the apartments themselves, I see others have mentioned the roaches, unfortunately this is true, creeping a long the floor, and they are huge! One of the apartments we had the sliding glass door had no security latch, we asked them to put one on, their response we don't have them in stock anymore so we aren't replacing them, okay, leave us unsafe, sound reasonable doesn't it? When we moved into our first apartment everything was dirty, filthy and stains and holes all over the carpeting, when we moved out we were charged for carpet cleaning. Since then they thought they'd cut costs and some upstairs apartments don't have carpeting, they have tile instead, talk about hearing every move your upstairs neighbors make. We had three kids above us that did nothing but jump, our entire apartment shook, kept letting the office know, they didn't care. We had to have a lot of maintenance done to our apartment which I previously mentioned were three weeks behind, you would put in your request and then instead of them coming they would send you an email stating that the work had been completed when they didn't even come, this was always happening. Then one morning I got out of bed and stepped into a huge puddle on the floor, ended up being a main pipe broke and flooded our two bedrooms and bathroom. It took them awhile to acknowledge the problem and then sent plumbers out to fix it. They never pulled up the carpeting that was all flooded out, talk about smelling moldy. We had people in and out of the apartment for days, and you would think with this that all the work could of been done, they  had to tear up some of the bathroom floor and put a huge hole in the bathroom wall, the work still wasn't completed by the time we moved out which was about three weeks or longer later. They did nothing to help the mold smell or anything. This happened in the second apartment, in the first apartment, the neighbors below us complained of squeaky floor board so instead of them giving us our notice maintenance came busting into our apartment immediately giving us no notice, it wasn't like the squeak had just begun and the floor was going to fall down, it had been that way for the 8 months we were in there before that. Anyways, they left and sent someone else to the apartment, I wasn't fully dressed and this guy comes barging into our apartment that wasn't even with the apartment complex, didn't knock or anything, I grabbed a blanket and covered myself, I'm like what are you doing, he said the office called him to come over and fix something, the guy had no idea why he was there or what he was suppose to fix but had the key to open the door and come in without us knowing he was coming or having our approval to enter the apartment. I went directly to the office to find out why they allowed this to happen and of course there was no answer by any of them. Thought I'd let you know these things are happening. There are a lot of pit bulls that live in these apartments and dogs that run around without leashes or without people watching them. I have been jumped on a few times by these dogs. There are also a huge amount of kids. One of my neighbors who has also lived there for a long time made a comment about it becoming a slum place and he said that others have been talking the same way. I actually did mention that to the office and they just brushed it off like don't be silly, but if you take a good look at it and look at the grounds really good before you move in then you might make the same decision. It use to be VERY VERY nice. Also if you use a cell phone be careful where you are moving in these apartments because you may not get signal. We had to live for a year without good signal and was very hard to make or receive calls so just be aware that this complex doesn't pick up signal very well and it's not a cheap cell phone company that we use, it's one of the major ones. Be aware that the office personnel don't know you by name but you are just a number to all of them and same with maintenance. The last thing be careful about payments to them, I sent them a check for the last portion of the move out and some how they are saying they didn't get it and sent me to collections. They didn't even try calling me to let me know they didn't receive it, off to collections I went. I had NEVER missed a rent payment or been late in the three years but off to collections I went. If you can overlook everything else, the apartments themselves aren't to bad as far as square footage but they are VERY expensive and not worth the headache or aggravation that is caused by them and the bad management. Please whatever you decide to do just remember we did try to warn you about this place.

reviews.review_text: If you’re considering living here, don’t. Unless, of course, you’re okay with sharing your home with rats, losing your furniture, and enduring sweltering heat with no real sense of urgency from management. We transferred units back in November 2024, and from the very beginning, we had a rat infestation. Rats — not one, not two, but a recurring, destructive infestation. Rats were underneath the fridge, within the back ends of the cabinets, and under appliances. The rodents would leave piles of feces in the cabinets, under our furniture, and on top of counter tops. Our house smells constantly of there feces or dead rats, no in between. No matter how much we cleaned or even got rid of the dead rats ourselves. Pest control showed up for about seven weeks, then stopped coming entirely. Even though they found rats each visit. The company told us that the management did not want to continue service until other units were reported. Predictably, the rats came back and of course It took yet another month for the complex to simply provide a response again in which was only a confirmation of the rat infestation once again and that only happened after my husband left a public review. They offered to help ONLY after panic calling my husband within minutes after the review to take it down. Apparently, ignoring tenant health and safety is standard practice until you threaten their reputation or legality. The rats caused actual resident property damage, they made a nest in our couch, ate through groceries within cabinets, pissed over our dishes and other stored items within cabinets and more. This has been a reoccurring issue with no actual solution, This has been thousands of dollars in personal loss, and not a single offer of compensation or meaningful help. They even wanted us to pay x2 our rent to even get out of the lease due to the rat infestation. Once again we are in the 7 week cycle and once again they will stop after the 7 week cycle and it will restart where we are going to need more residents besides us to put in a report about the rat infestation for them to come back and do another cycle. It will be an endless cycle until we can get out of the lease. Now, let’s talk about the AC — or lack thereof. Our air conditioning has had problems since we moved In. During the winter it went out quite a few times and we submitted maintenance requests. It was eventually temporarily fixed for the winter. We were told the unit would stop working as it is fairly old. The unit was not replaced or treated again until now during the summer. It stopped working on a Saturday night and since then we have spent every night in up to 90 degree interior temperature. Someone finally came Monday only to confirm the entire unit was dead and had to be replaced. Once again telling us the unit is going to stop working and needing to be replaced. In the meantime their temporary solution was A single portable AC unit. The interior temperature did not change it was still 90+ degrees in every room. WE told the maintenance the solution was not working and we needed either another solution or something alternative. Not a great solution that is until the power went out immediately after the technician left. I tried calling the office for over an hour and was sent straight to voicemail every single time. My husband had to physically go down to the office to get any sort of response. Their solution? Offer another portable unit. But — surprise — the maintenance team was already gone. We sat for over two hours in a hot, powerless apartment before anyone came to help. This place is a masterclass in negligence. There is no urgency, no accountability, and certainly no regard for the health, comfort, or sanity of the people who live here. Every “solution” they offer feels half-hearted and delayed to the point of being useless. If this is how they handle basic habitability issues — rodents, air conditioning, electricity — imagine how they treat anything else. It’s not just frustrating. It’s unacceptable.

reviews.author: JSM2015
reviews.review_text:
Here's what you need to know about Finisterra & its management company, Milestone Management. 

- The staff in the leasing office do not even pretend to care about your problems. At best, they are pleasant & dismissive . At worst, they are argumentative, condescending & utterly useless. Do not ever go into that office thinking that they will help to advocate for your needs as a paying resident.

- After a few short months of residency, I quickly lost my sense of safety in the complex. Several violent break-ins occurred in the complex in the year we lived there. We were woken up to the SWAT team kicking us out of our apartment on one occasion while in pursuit of an armed suspect who was lurking in the complex. The office does not update the community when break-ins occur to help with awareness, as there were several incidents & only one letter issued after it was obvious that Finisterra had already been all over the news. 

- Intel rents close to half of these apartments out to workers moving here from out of the country. What this leads to is a large population of foreign people that congregate in the common areas & basically take it over & neighbors that make loud overseas phone calls on their patios or while pacing the walkways at all hours of the night.
It's clear that it's just a temporary landing pad for them to get settled- most of them have patio sets in their living rooms or nothing at all. I completely understand their situation, it's nothing against them. But for people wanting to live in a relaxing neighborhood setting, Finisterra is not the place. it feels more like a hostile or a temporary residency motel.  

- Unless there is a flood or a toilet issue maintenance will not be issued to your unit in a timely manner. It was not uncommon for work orders to be completely forgotten. The average was about 5 days to a week, with my calling everyday to ensure the work order was still on the agenda. The maintenance team are nice enough people & the fixes are usually quick but you are regarded as such a hassle when the issue really is the cheap, old equipment. 
At one point our roof leaked & a bucket sat in my living room for two days. The drywall was destroyed in the living room & bathroom & it took them months to come repaint it. It was so embarrassing when guests would come over & we looked like people who didn't bother to maintain their home or couldn't afford for proper upkeep. Issues like this would go unresolved with no regard or sense of urgency from Finisterra. The last few months of our stay we basically stopped trying to get any non-essential issued fix & just lived with it. We were sick of the fight. I understand that my needs cannot always be meet immediately, but to live daily in an environment that is being neglected is a total bummer- & yet I'm still obligated to pay my rent in full every month.  

- Looking towards the positive, I can say Finisterra is beautifully maintained on the outside- & that's about it. I am happy to no longer be under contract with them. If this review can convince one person to pass on this complex (& hopefully any Milestone Management-run facility) than at least my misfortune may have saved one person from my same sufferings! For real.

reviews.review_text: Overall, Finisterra is pretty nice. The grounds are kept pretty nice, the staff is pretty nice (barring one of the front desk employees, more about that later), and the residents are pretty nice. The single worst we experienced at Finisterra was getting the security deposit back. My god. We moved out in SEPTEMBER. We just received the correct amount THIS LAST WEEK. Do you see the date of this review? Weâ€™re almost at the end of March. Iâ€™m not exaggerating when I say we called the office 20+ times. Every time we called we were assured that they would talk to management. Multiple times we were sent the wrong amount. Legally, in AZ, youâ€™re supposed to receive your deposit within two weeks of moving out. If itâ€™s not returned to you within that time, you can go to small claims court and submit a claim to get x2 your deposit back. For one of my calls last month, I threatened them with going this route. Surprise, it didnâ€™t matter to them. I should have just filed the claim due to the sheer amount of our time they wasted and the fact that we left the apartment in better shape that we found it. We even asked, what about the damage that was there when we moved in, did the last person get charged for that as well? Radio silence on their end. 5 months later we got the security deposit back. Ridiculous. The second worst thing weâ€™ve experienced at Finisterra was actually our move-in day. We were first time movers, so looking back we were a bit naive and should have said something. But in our defense, we had a full rental truck and an army of movers waiting soâ€¦ When we arrived at the office on our move-in date, they were simply not ready for us. We had to wait 45 minutes (with our friends and family who were moving us) to get the keys ready. This was in June. Once we got the keys, it was obvious that they also didnâ€™t get the apartment ready for us either â€“ it wasnâ€™t clean. There was clear evidence that the renters before us had a black cat. There was black cat hair everywhereâ€“I am allergic to cats. I was still cleaning up cat hair 14 months later. Also, there was human hair (like beard clippings) in the bathroom cabinets. The toilets werenâ€™t clean. Some of the bathroom and kitchen cabinets smelled like cat food months later. The floors were not clean, it left our feet dirty enough that we made a special trip to Walmart and bought a mop that very first day. The apartment complex is consistently covered with dog poop (not exactly not-the-norm, but the apartment could do more than just encouraging people to pick up dog poop in a friendly email) and rats roam around. The third worst thing was the package delivery system. We paid $15 a month forâ€¦nothing. In fact, they closed the parcel lockers at the mail area so any packages (Amazon, online shopping, etc) got sent directly to the post office down the street. A little inconvenient, but hurts more when youâ€™re paying for something that you donâ€™t get the service of. My mail actually got stolen from my mailbox (a Christmas card from my parents for christâ€™s sakeâ€¦) but the office quickly fixed my mailbox. The mail man was consistently leaving our mailbox open for all to take. So, I would be a little wary of having important things sent. We never had anything stolen from our door, however, and we were facing one of the parking lots. The fourth worst thing we experienced was when they decided to renew our lease for us, which was interesting to say the least. Especially since our type of units were going for $200/month less. We actually went into the office and discussed the possibility of lowering our lease for when we renewed it, since our units were currently going for cheaper at the time. The employee, Angalique, said sheâ€™d email corporate and let us know what the response was. After calling to ask a month later, still no response. By the time we moved out, our apartment was still going for $200/month less and they were still calling us about renewing at our current lease price. The trash system is fine. That is included in the fees (not a part of rent) and you cannot get out of it. But, this means people just leave trash on their porch when theyâ€™re not really supposed to. We had our neighbor (who we shared an entrance with) leave her dogâ€™s pee pads outside of the door in the summer sun all day which became pretty aromatic to come home to. The grounds are kept generally clean. Thereâ€™s always dog poop everywhere, but Iâ€™m pretty sure thatâ€™s with every complex. They did send out an complex-wide email that reminded people that their porches cannot be used as a storage unit and to clean up after the dog poop (at least x3). That was nice to see. Maintenance is pretty responsive, but some of our problems are still not fixed a month after we put the request in (blinds not working). Our neighbors had to have their sewer/plumbing worked on and they used a jackhammer on the sidewalk outside of the door to get under the concrete. 8 months later they have yet to fill it up with something other than dirt. The apartment we were in was renovated and was really nice. I like the hardwood floors (second floor), countertops, and patio. The patio is a huge part of the apartment and was the biggest patio we saw in our search. Every one of our friends and family who saw it were pretty amazed. The admin office is very responsive. There was a resident who left their dogs with separation anxiety on the porch for a trip, who were barking all through the day and night. I messaged the admins and they quickly resolved the situation. They also forgot to add in the month-off deal to our lease so we went into the office to inquire. The employee, a young man (sorry I donâ€™t remember his name) was very apologetic and super nice. That was a nice interaction. The only problem I had was when we went to discuss renewing with the front office employee, Angalique, who seemed like she didnâ€™t want to be there and was rude to us when we asked about renewing our lease. Iâ€™m not one to call employees out much but that left a lasting impression. I didnâ€™t want to speak with her again. She shouldnâ€™t work there. The pools are pretty small, so expect them to be filled with kids in the summertime. Not really the apartmentâ€™s fault, but donâ€™t expect quiet hours during that time. The area around the apartment is fine, the two highlights are the Walmart 0.1 miles away and the Costco 0.2 miles away. South mountain is right there for hiking, and the I10 is right there for commuters. When we moved out, we left it cleaner than when we found it. We were still charged $150 for cleaning. Upon inquiring about the itemized bill, we magically got half off. Then, when they sent us pictures of what they cleaned and it was actually from the previous resident. So, it seems like they donâ€™t clean the places, say that they did, and then still charge the next resident for not cleaning it. Weâ€™re waiting on a reply from management to see whether or not they billed the previous residents as well. Also, it looks like they try to charge for normal wear and tear (paint and baseboard touchups), which they canâ€™t do. Itâ€™s against the law. We also returned our keys a month earlier and got a call a month later saying we didnâ€™t return our keys and that we didnâ€™t return them and we would be billed. They called us multiple times about that and we explained multiple times that we in fact had turned in the keys and we had photos. That eventually stopped after they were finally able to figure it out. Seems like they canâ€™t find the keys when you get there and when you leaveâ€¦ Overall, the complex is fine and the apartments are quite nice. I would say the crowd is more families than not, which can be good or bad in peopleâ€™s eyes. I wouldnâ€™t say Iâ€™d be happy next to the grass fields with the playing kids but some might be. Would I live here again? Before the deposit fiasco, I would have said probably. The cons werenâ€™t enough to keep me from coming back, but Iâ€™d be selective about what building I was in in regards to some areas and to be wary of the lease price. It fluctuates a lot. But after the whole ordeal with management, seeing how incompetent they are (except Harry, thanks Harry), Iâ€™m not sure I would go back. reviews.review_text: I moved into Finisterra in 2022 and loved living here when it was managed by Greystar. However, since the Preferred Apartment Communities (PAC) team took over the complex in early 2023, the complex has gone drastically downhill. Here is a list of issues that have happened since PAC took over: -Crime: Three of my neighbor's vehicles were broken into and multiple packages were stolen. The Greystar team used to hire security to walk around the complex at night to prevent break ins. The PAC team cut security out (even though our rent and fees increased), and break ins have significantly increased. -Amenities & Grounds: Since PAC took over, the pool and hot tub were closed for 2.5 months, and the gym was closed for 2 months. The gates have been broken over 50% of the time (which doesn't help with crime either) and the fire pit was closed for over 6 months. The lawn used to be beautiful with healthy grass and plants. It has now been replaced with dirt and dying plants that aren't watered. They didn't even bother to respond to the emails or voicemails I sent asking to give us some money back on our rent due to the amenities being closed. When we went in person to ask, they said that since there wasn't an amenity fee at the time, they could choose to close the amenities at any time and wouldn't be reducing rent in any form. The amenities were the primary reason that I (and several other residents) chose this complex. -'Paint Fee' - Beware that when you move out, you will receive a significant paint fee which will cause you to get less than half of your security deposit back. Even if the condition of your walls is perfect, you will still be charged this fee (I was actually told this by one of the employees). As it is not in the lease under fees you will be charged upon move out, I have been trying to contact someone for over 1.5 months to have this reimbursed. To this date, I have not received a single email or phone call from the manger regarding this (even though I was promised 4 times that the manager would reach out to me next day). After reading other reviews, other residents also seem to have been scammed by this 'paint fee' and ghosted by the PAC team when trying to inquire about the fee. -Move out date: Make sure your lease end date isn't on a date the office is closed. The last day of my lease was on the 14th of January, and I wanted to move out this date. The office was closed the 14th because it was a Sunday, and also closed the 15th for MLK Jr. Day. I was told I either had to move out the 13th (and still pay for the 14th) or pay to extend the lease and move out the 16th since the office doesn't have a drop box for keys. I was also told I had to pay extra fees if I were to stay beyond the 14th. To avoid additional fees, I was forced to move out the 13th and still had to pay for a day of rent that I didn't even get. I'm honestly not sure if this is even legal, but the PAC team did not care. -Communication: If you have a grievance or issue, you will need to go in person to the office to talk to the PAC team as they ignore emails and phone calls. When they do rarely answer the phone, they tell you they will call you back with an answer (& they never call back). I would highly recommend avoiding this apartment complex due to the issues listed above.
